new.md:
Creates a new `GtkViewport`.

The new viewport uses the given adjustments, or default
adjustments if none are given.

doc.brief: Implements scrollability for widgets that don't support scrolling on their own.
doc.md:
Implements scrollability for widgets that don't support scrolling
on their own.

Use `GtkViewport` to scroll child widgets such as `GtkGrid`,
`GtkBox`, and so on.

The `GtkViewport` will start scrolling content only if allocated
less than the child widget’s minimum size in a given orientation.

# CSS nodes

`GtkViewport` has a single CSS node with name `viewport`.

# Accessibility

Until GTK 4.10, `GtkViewport` used the [`AccessibleRole.group`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AccessibleRole#value:group) role.

Starting from GTK 4.12, `GtkViewport` uses the [`AccessibleRole.generic`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AccessibleRole#value:generic) role.

get_scroll_to_focus.brief: Gets whether the viewport is scrolling to keep the focused child in view.
get_scroll_to_focus.md:
Gets whether the viewport is scrolling to keep the focused
child in view.

scroll_to.brief: Scrolls a descendant of the viewport into view.
scroll_to.md:
Scrolls a descendant of the viewport into view.

The viewport and the descendant must be visible and mapped for
this function to work, otherwise no scrolling will be performed.

set_scroll_to_focus.brief: Sets whether the viewport should automatically scroll to keep the focused child in view.
set_scroll_to_focus.md:
Sets whether the viewport should automatically scroll
to keep the focused child in view.

scroll-to-focus.brief: Whether to scroll when the focus changes.
scroll-to-focus.md:
Whether to scroll when the focus changes.

Before 4.6.2, this property was mistakenly defaulting to FALSE, so if your
code needs to work with older versions, consider setting it explicitly to
TRUE.
